**Guang'an** (simplified Chinese: 广安; traditional Chinese: 廣安; pinyin: *Guǎng'ān*; Wade–Giles: *kwang-an*) is a prefecture-level city in eastern Sichuan province. It is most famous as the birthplace of China's former paramount leader Deng Xiaoping. Guang'an lies between the hills of central Sichuan and the gorges area of the east. Guang'an is the only "Sichuan Chongqing Cooperation Demonstration Zone" in Sichuan and the nearest prefecture level city from the main city of Chongqing. It has been incorporated into the 1 hour economic circle of Chongqing. Because of its strategic location, it is called the "Gateway to Eastern Sichuan". Its population, as of the 2020 census, was 3,254,883, of whom 976,370 lived in the built-up (*or metro*) area made up of 2 urban districts.

<document>
<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

During the Chinese Civil War, Huang'an County (as it was then known) was a stronghold of the Chinese Communist Party. It was in Huang'an where in November 1927 Communist guerrillas founded the first peasants' government that would eventually evolve into the future Eyuwan soviet. It was also the location where Communist General Xu Haidong founded the Seventh Red Army with a handful of recruits.[1] From the core of Huang'an, Macheng, and Guangshan counties, the Eyuwan Soviet would gradually expand to become the second-largest soviet republic in China, with over one million inhabitants.[2] The Red Army units based in Eyuwan recruited heavily from Huang'an, and many natives of the county went on to serve in high ranks of the People's Liberation Army. In the early 1950s, over 200 PLA generals hailed from Huang'an. Two of these men, Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, both would go on to serve as President of the People's Republic of China.[3]



## Geography

[edit]

### Administrative divisions

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>
In 845 BC, Marquis Wen (文侯) Huang Meng (黃孟) (aka Huang Zhang; 黃璋) moved the capital of the State of Huang from Yicheng to Huangchuan (present-day Huangchuan, Henan). Huang Xi's descendants ruled the State of Huang until 648 BC when it was destroyed and conquered by the State of Chu. The Marquis of Huang, Marquis Mu (穆侯) Huang Qisheng (黃企生), fled to the state of Qi. The people of Huang were forced to relocate to Chu. They settled in the region of present-day Hubei province, in a region known as the Jiangxia Commandery (江夏郡) during the Han dynasty (206 BC-AD 220). There are many places in this region today that were named after Huang e.g. Huanggang, Huangpi, Huangmei, Huangshi, Huang'an (now Hong'an), Huangzhou etc. A large number of the people of Huang were also relocated to regions south of the Yangtze River.

<document>
<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.




## History

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>

During the Chinese Civil War, Huang'an County (as it was then known) was a stronghold of the Chinese Communist Party. It was in Huang'an where in November 1927 Communist guerrillas founded the first peasants' government that would eventually evolve into the future Eyuwan soviet. It was also the location where Communist General Xu Haidong founded the Seventh Red Army with a handful of recruits.[1] From the core of Huang'an, Macheng, and Guangshan counties, the Eyuwan Soviet would gradually expand to become the second-largest soviet republic in China, with over one million inhabitants.[2] The Red Army units based in Eyuwan recruited heavily from Huang'an, and many natives of the county went on to serve in high ranks of the People's Liberation Army. In the early 1950s, over 200 PLA generals hailed from Huang'an. Two of these men, Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, both would go on to serve as President of the People's Republic of China.[3]

<document>
<title>Deng Xiaoping</title>
<fragment>
![](image)Deng Xiaoping at age 16, studying in France (1921)
Deng's ancestors can be traced back to Jiaying County (now renamed as Meixian), Guangdong,[12] a prominent ancestral area for the Hakka people, and had settled in Sichuan for several generations.[13] Deng's daughter Deng Rong wrote in the book *My Father Deng Xiaoping* (我的父亲邓小平) that his ancestry was probably, but not definitely, Hakka. Sichuan was originally the origin of the Deng lineage until one of them was hired as an official in Guangdong during the Ming dynasty, but when the Qing dynasty planned to increase the population in 1671, they moved back to Sichuan. Deng was born in Guang'an District, Guang'an on 22 August 1904 in Sichuan province.[14]


</fragment>
<fragment>
After leaving the army of Feng Yuxiang in the northwest, Deng ended up in the city of Wuhan, where the Communists at that time had their headquarters. At that time, he began using the nickname "Xiaoping" and occupied prominent positions in the party apparatus. He participated in the historic emergency session on 7 August 1927 in which, by Soviet instruction, the Party dismissed its founder Chen Duxiu, and Qu Qiubai became the general secretary. In Wuhan, Deng first established contact with Mao Zedong, who was then little valued by militant pro-Soviet leaders of the party.


Between 1927 and 1929, Deng lived in Shanghai, where he helped organize protests that would be harshly persecuted by the Kuomintang authorities. The death of many Communist militants in those years led to a decrease in the number of members of the Communist Party, which enabled Deng to quickly move up the ranks. During this stage in Shanghai, Deng married a woman he met in Moscow, Zhang Xiyuan.



### Military campaign in Guangxi

[edit]

A bronze statue to commemorate Deng's 100th birthday was dedicated 13 August 2004 in the city of Guang'an, Deng's hometown, in southwest China's Sichuan. Deng is dressed casually, sitting on a chair and smiling. The Chinese characters on the pedestal were written by Jiang Zemin, then General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party and Chairman of the Central Military Commission.[131]


Deng Xiaoping's Former Residence in his hometown of Paifang Village in Sichuan has been preserved as an historical museum.

The **Former Residence of Deng Xiaoping** (simplified Chinese: 邓小平故居; traditional Chinese: 鄧小平故居; pinyin: *Dèng Xiǎopíng Gùjū*) was built in the late Qing dynasty (19th century). It is located in Paifang Village of Xiexing Town, Guang'an District, Guang'an City, Sichuan, China.[1][2] It has a building area of about 833.4 m2 (8,971 sq ft), embodies buildings such as the old houses, the statue of Deng Xiaoping, the Dezheng Place (德政坊), the Cultural relics Exhibition Hall, the Hanlin Yard (翰林院子).[3]



## History

[edit]

In the late Qing dynasty (19th century), the house was built by Deng Xiaoping's great-grandfather Deng Xinzao (邓心早) and grandfather Deng Keda (邓克达).[*citation needed*]


Deng Xiaoping was born here on 22 August 1904, in the 37th year of the Guangxu reign. He lived here for about 15 years.[4]


In July 1997, it was listed as a National Patriotic Education Base by the Central Propaganda Department of the Chinese Communist Party.[*citation needed*]


In February 1998, the General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party Jiang Zemin wrote "Deng Xiaoping's Former Residence" on the horizontal tablet.[*citation needed*]


On 25 June 2001, it was listed as a Major Historical and Cultural Site Protected at the National Level by the State Council of the People's Republic of China.[*citation needed*]


On 13 August 2004, the CCP general secretary Hu Jintao attended the unveiling of the statue of Deng Xiaoping.[4]

<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

<fragment>

During the Chinese Civil War, Huang'an County (as it was then known) was a stronghold of the Chinese Communist Party. It was in Huang'an where in November 1927 Communist guerrillas founded the first peasants' government that would eventually evolve into the future Eyuwan soviet. It was also the location where Communist General Xu Haidong founded the Seventh Red Army with a handful of recruits.[1] From the core of Huang'an, Macheng, and Guangshan counties, the Eyuwan Soviet would gradually expand to become the second-largest soviet republic in China, with over one million inhabitants.[2] The Red Army units based in Eyuwan recruited heavily from Huang'an, and many natives of the county went on to serve in high ranks of the People's Liberation Army. In the early 1950s, over 200 PLA generals hailed from Huang'an. Two of these men, Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, both would go on to serve as President of the People's Republic of China.[3]

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

During the Chinese Civil War, Huang'an County (as it was then known) was a stronghold of the Chinese Communist Party. It was in Huang'an where in November 1927 Communist guerrillas founded the first peasants' government that would eventually evolve into the future Eyuwan soviet. It was also the location where Communist General Xu Haidong founded the Seventh Red Army with a handful of recruits.[1] From the core of Huang'an, Macheng, and Guangshan counties, the Eyuwan Soviet would gradually expand to become the second-largest soviet republic in China, with over one million inhabitants.[2] The Red Army units based in Eyuwan recruited heavily from Huang'an, and many natives of the county went on to serve in high ranks of the People's Liberation Army. In the early 1950s, over 200 PLA generals hailed from Huang'an. Two of these men, Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, both would go on to serve as President of the People's Republic of China.[3]

<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

After returning to Beijing, Xie played a key role in providing military weapons to favored Red Guard factions, including the supply of 500 rifles to the Jinggangshan Commune of Beijing's Teacher's University.[4]: 289



## Legacy

[edit]

Xie died before the denunciation of the Gang of Four in 1976, but he was identified in official documents, along with Kang Sheng, as equally responsible for the excesses of the Cultural Revolution and guilty of "anti-party activities". He was posthumously expelled from the Party in 1980 and his ashes were removed from the Babaoshan Revolutionary Cemetery.[*citation needed*]

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

During the Chinese Civil War, Huang'an County (as it was then known) was a stronghold of the Chinese Communist Party. It was in Huang'an where in November 1927 Communist guerrillas founded the first peasants' government that would eventually evolve into the future Eyuwan soviet. It was also the location where Communist General Xu Haidong founded the Seventh Red Army with a handful of recruits.[1] From the core of Huang'an, Macheng, and Guangshan counties, the Eyuwan Soviet would gradually expand to become the second-largest soviet republic in China, with over one million inhabitants.[2] The Red Army units based in Eyuwan recruited heavily from Huang'an, and many natives of the county went on to serve in high ranks of the People's Liberation Army. In the early 1950s, over 200 PLA generals hailed from Huang'an. Two of these men, Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, both would go on to serve as President of the People's Republic of China.[3]

<title>Eyuwan Soviet</title>
<fragment>
Despite its convoluted history, the Fourth Red Army became one of the most important sources of officers for later CCP military units. It was one of the main sources of the soldiers who served in the New Fourth Army.[63] Even by the 1950s, "70 percent of cadres at the divisional level and above in the People's Liberation Army were natives of Eyuwan."[64] Just one county, Huang'an, was the home of over 200 PLA generals. Huang'an was also the home of Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, both of whom would serve as President of the People's Republic of China.[65]


Nonetheless, the historiography of Eyuwan in the People's Republic of China was largely negative for many years.[63] Zhang Guotao defected from the CCP in 1938 and joined the Nationalists. Given Zhang's association with Eyuwan, this greatly damaged the regions reputation and most early assessments focused criticism on the excessiveness of Zhang's purges.[51]

The first "peasants' government" in the Eyuwan region was founded in Huang'an County in November 1927. There, Xu Haidong also founded the Seventh Red Army with a handful of recruits.[9] However, the Communists remained mobile, having to stay on the run from Nationalist armies. They slowly built up a following in the counties of Huang'an, Macheng, and Guangshan as the army passed through villages, organizing peasants as it went.[4] They were helped by the fact that the Nationalists could not devote their full military strength to crushing the Communists. They were dealing with the Chiang-Gui War and the rebellion of a local officer in Macheng.[10] In the summer of 1929, the consolidated their first permanent territory in Macheng near the mountain pass of Songziguan (松子关). From here, they were able to start land redistribution. 
</fragment>
<fragment>
One popular destination for fleeing Communists was the Dabie Mountains, a border region between Hubei, Henan, and Anhui provinces (the "Eyuwan" region). Many Communists were in fact natives of this region and had been sent by their parents to study in the cities. By returning to their native region, they could count on family ties as a recruitment tool.[4] But while the rugged terrain gave them shelter from the Nationalist armies, it provided the same benefit for bandit gangs.[5] The highlands of Eyuwan had been plagued by roaming bandits for centuries, leading local communities to develop strong self-defense organizations known as Red Spear Societies.[6] There was considerable local variation between different Red Spear Societies; in western Henan they were hardly distinguishable from bandits themselves, whereas in the east they were fiercely loyal to the local gentry.[7] But in both cases, they were initially hostile to the Communists.

<document>
<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.




## History

In 845 BC, Marquis Wen (文侯) Huang Meng (黃孟) (aka Huang Zhang; 黃璋) moved the capital of the State of Huang from Yicheng to Huangchuan (present-day Huangchuan, Henan). Huang Xi's descendants ruled the State of Huang until 648 BC when it was destroyed and conquered by the State of Chu. The Marquis of Huang, Marquis Mu (穆侯) Huang Qisheng (黃企生), fled to the state of Qi. The people of Huang were forced to relocate to Chu. They settled in the region of present-day Hubei province, in a region known as the Jiangxia Commandery (江夏郡) during the Han dynasty (206 BC-AD 220). There are many places in this region today that were named after Huang e.g. Huanggang, Huangpi, Huangmei, Huangshi, Huang'an (now Hong'an), Huangzhou etc. A large number of the people of Huang were also relocated to regions south of the Yangtze River.


</fragment>
<fragment>

During the Chinese Civil War, Huang'an County (as it was then known) was a stronghold of the Chinese Communist Party. It was in Huang'an where in November 1927 Communist guerrillas founded the first peasants' government that would eventually evolve into the future Eyuwan soviet. It was also the location where Communist General Xu Haidong founded the Seventh Red Army with a handful of recruits.[1] From the core of Huang'an, Macheng, and Guangshan counties, the Eyuwan Soviet would gradually expand to become the second-largest soviet republic in China, with over one million inhabitants.[2] The Red Army units based in Eyuwan recruited heavily from Huang'an, and many natives of the county went on to serve in high ranks of the People's Liberation Army. In the early 1950s, over 200 PLA generals hailed from Huang'an. Two of these men, Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, both would go on to serve as President of the People's Republic of China.[3]

<title>Huanggang</title>
<fragment>
* Huang Kan (黄侃), a Chinese philologist.


As well, Huanggang is famous for producing military and political leaders. Hong'an County is known as the "County of Generals" in that more than 400 Chinese army generals have been born there, a total far greater than for any other county in all of China. In addition, former military leader and President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an. The family of Taiwanese author Kuo Cheng came from Huanggang.[11]

In 845 BC Marquis Wen (文侯) Huang Meng (黃孟; also known as Huang Zhang / 黃璋) moved the capital of the State of Huang from Yicheng to Huangchuan (present-day Huangchuan, Henan). Huang Xi's descendants ruled State of Huang until 648 BC when it was destroyed by the State of Chu. The Marquis of Huang, Marquis Mu (穆侯) Huang Qisheng (黃企生), fled to the state of Qi. The people of Huang were forced to relocate to Chu. They settled in the region of present-day Hubei province, in a region known as the Jiangxia Prefecture (江夏郡) during the Han dynasty (206 BC-AD 220). There are many places in this region today that were named after Huang e.g. Huanggang, Huangpi, Huangmei, Huangshi, Huangan, Huangzhou etc. Many of the people of Huang were also relocated to regions south of the Yangtze River.

<document>
<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

<document>
<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

The **Former Residence of Deng Xiaoping** (simplified Chinese: 邓小平故居; traditional Chinese: 鄧小平故居; pinyin: *Dèng Xiǎopíng Gùjū*) was built in the late Qing dynasty (19th century). It is located in Paifang Village of Xiexing Town, Guang'an District, Guang'an City, Sichuan, China.[1][2] It has a building area of about 833.4 m2 (8,971 sq ft), embodies buildings such as the old houses, the statue of Deng Xiaoping, the Dezheng Place (德政坊), the Cultural relics Exhibition Hall, the Hanlin Yard (翰林院子).[3]



## History

[edit]

In the late Qing dynasty (19th century), the house was built by Deng Xiaoping's great-grandfather Deng Xinzao (邓心早) and grandfather Deng Keda (邓克达).[*citation needed*]


Deng Xiaoping was born here on 22 August 1904, in the 37th year of the Guangxu reign. He lived here for about 15 years.[4]


In July 1997, it was listed as a National Patriotic Education Base by the Central Propaganda Department of the Chinese Communist Party.[*citation needed*]


In February 1998, the General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party Jiang Zemin wrote "Deng Xiaoping's Former Residence" on the horizontal tablet.[*citation needed*]


On 25 June 2001, it was listed as a Major Historical and Cultural Site Protected at the National Level by the State Council of the People's Republic of China.[*citation needed*]


On 13 August 2004, the CCP general secretary Hu Jintao attended the unveiling of the statue of Deng Xiaoping.[4]



## References

3. **^** Qiu Tian (March 22, 2018). 走进小平故里 接受红色洗礼. *china.com* (in Chinese).
4. ^ ***a*** ***b*** 图说广安邓小平故居：04年胡锦涛为小平铜像揭幕(1/7). *Phoenix Television* (in Chinese). Retrieved May 2, 2013.

Based on my comprehensive searches through Wikipedia and related sources, here is what I have been able to determine about Li Xiannian's connections to Qiliping Town and Hong'an County:

## **Confirmed Information:**

### **1. Li Xiannian's Birthplace**
- **Li Xiannian (1909-1992)** was definitely **born in Hong'an County** (红安县), Hubei Province
- Hong'an County is famous as the "County of the Generals" - over 200 PLA generals came from this area
- Hong'an County is administered by Huanggang City (黄冈市)

### **2. Qiliping Town Connection**
- **Qiliping Town (七里坪镇)** is one of the 10 towns within Hong'an County
- The town covers **351.33 square kilometers**, making it one of the largest towns in the county
- **Qiliping Revolutionary Sites** (七里坪革命旧址) are listed as a **Major National Historical and Cultural Site** (3rd batch, #24)
- This confirms Qiliping's historical significance during the revolutionary period when Li Xiannian was active

### **3. Major Historical Sites**
From the official list of protected sites in Hubei:

**A. Qiliping Revolutionary Sites (七里坪革命旧址)**
- **Location**: Hong'an County 
- **Protection Level**: National (3rd batch designation)
- **Significance**: Indicates major revolutionary historical importance

**B. Former Residence of Li Xiannian (李先念故居)**
- **Location**: Hong'an County
- **Protection Level**: National Historical and Cultural Site (6th batch, 2006, #992)

## **Key Findings:**

### **Strong Historical Connection:**
The fact that both Li Xiannian's former residence AND Qiliping revolutionary sites are national-level protected historical sites strongly suggests they are related or possibly co-located. The timing of these designations (Qiliping sites in earlier batch, Li Xiannian residence in 2006) indicates their recognized historical importance.

### **Likely Location:**
While I cannot definitively confirm that Li Xiannian was born within the current boundaries of Qiliping Town, the convergence of:
- His birth in Hong'an County
- Qiliping's revolutionary significance
- Both sites being national-level protected historical monuments
- Qiliping being a major town in the county

...strongly suggests his birthplace is either within Qiliping Town or very closely associated with it.

- **Exact village name** where Li Xiannian was born

- **Coordinates** or detailed addresses of memorial sites
- **Specific descriptions** of monuments or commemorative facilities
- **Tourism infrastructure** information

To find the specific village name and detailed location information you're seeking, I recommend searching:

<document>
<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

[edit]

<fragment>

During the Chinese Civil War, Huang'an County (as it was then known) was a stronghold of the Chinese Communist Party. It was in Huang'an where in November 1927 Communist guerrillas founded the first peasants' government that would eventually evolve into the future Eyuwan soviet. It was also the location where Communist General Xu Haidong founded the Seventh Red Army with a handful of recruits.[1] From the core of Huang'an, Macheng, and Guangshan counties, the Eyuwan Soviet would gradually expand to become the second-largest soviet republic in China, with over one million inhabitants.[2] The Red Army units based in Eyuwan recruited heavily from Huang'an, and many natives of the county went on to serve in high ranks of the People's Liberation Army. In the early 1950s, over 200 PLA generals hailed from Huang'an. Two of these men, Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, both would go on to serve as President of the People's Republic of China.[3]

Despite its convoluted history, the Fourth Red Army became one of the most important sources of officers for later CCP military units. It was one of the main sources of the soldiers who served in the New Fourth Army.[63] Even by the 1950s, "70 percent of cadres at the divisional level and above in the People's Liberation Army were natives of Eyuwan."[64] Just one county, Huang'an, was the home of over 200 PLA generals. Huang'an was also the home of Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, both of whom would serve as President of the People's Republic of China.[65]


Nonetheless, the historiography of Eyuwan in the People's Republic of China was largely negative for many years.[63] Zhang Guotao defected from the CCP in 1938 and joined the Nationalists. In this period, Dong came to be known as one of the *Five Elders of Yan'an* (Chinese: 延安五老), along with Lin Boqu, Xu Teli, Wu Yuzhang, and Xie Juezai.


During the war with Japan, Dong divided his time between Wuhan and Chongqing as a liaison with the Nationalist government, given his previous Kuomintang associations. In 1945, he traveled to San Francisco to attend the founding session of the United Nations, as part of a delegation led by T.V. Soong.[3] He was the only representative of the Communist Party, whose Central Committee outlined the objectives of the trip as follows: "to win foreign friends, to improve the party's international position, and to try to stay and work in the United States."[4] After the conference, Dong spent several months traveling the United States, seeking to attain these diplomatic goals. Towards the end of the Civil War in 1948, following decisive victories in the north, Dong was appointed Chairman of the North China People's Government.

<document>
<title>Eyuwan Soviet</title>
<fragment>
Despite its convoluted history, the Fourth Red Army became one of the most important sources of officers for later CCP military units. It was one of the main sources of the soldiers who served in the New Fourth Army.[63] Even by the 1950s, "70 percent of cadres at the divisional level and above in the People's Liberation Army were natives of Eyuwan."[64] Just one county, Huang'an, was the home of over 200 PLA generals. Huang'an was also the home of Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, both of whom would serve as President of the People's Republic of China.[65]


Nonetheless, the historiography of Eyuwan in the People's Republic of China was largely negative for many years.[63] Zhang Guotao defected from the CCP in 1938 and joined the Nationalists. Given Zhang's association with Eyuwan, this greatly damaged the regions reputation and most early assessments focused criticism on the excessiveness of Zhang's purges.[51]



## Notes

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>
1. **^** Chinese: 鄂豫皖苏维埃; pinyin: *Èyùwǎn Sūwéi'āi*. The name comes from the Chinese abbreviations of Hubei (*È*), Henan (*Yù*), and Anhui (*Wǎn*). It's also known as the **Hubei–Henan–Anhui Soviet** or the **Eyuwan Revolutionary Base Area** (鄂豫皖革命根据地第; *Èyùwǎn gémìng gēnjùdì dì*).

## References

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>
The first "peasants' government" in the Eyuwan region was founded in Huang'an County in November 1927. There, Xu Haidong also founded the Seventh Red Army with a handful of recruits.[9] However, the Communists remained mobile, having to stay on the run from Nationalist armies. They slowly built up a following in the counties of Huang'an, Macheng, and Guangshan as the army passed through villages, organizing peasants as it went.[4] They were helped by the fact that the Nationalists could not devote their full military strength to crushing the Communists. They were dealing with the Chiang-Gui War and the rebellion of a local officer in Macheng.[10] In the summer of 1929, the consolidated their first permanent territory in Macheng near the mountain pass of Songziguan (松子关). From here, they were able to start land redistribution. 
</fragment>
<fragment>

The disconnected Communist bases in the Dabie mountains continued to hold out well until late 1934. However, in November Xu Haidong was defeated and fled with the Twenty-fifth Red Army towards the Shaanxi-Sichuan base area.[58] Nationalist commander Liang Guanying (梁冠英) was given 170,000 men to exterminate the remaining guerilla forces in Eyuwan. His system of checkpoints and blockhouses failed because the Communists were able to mobilize their supporters among the local peasantry to slow construction and bypass checkpoints.[60] Liang was replaced with Wei Lihuang. Wei had significantly more troops, and also made use of concentration camps to deprive the Communists of peasant support.[61] Despite occasional victories, the Communists were in the main defeated by this strategy. Most of the remaining guerrillas abandoned open warfare and began to operate undercover amongst the peasants. Until the Second United Front began in 1937, the Communists in Eyuwan were on the edge of collapse.[62]



## Legacy

[edit]


</fragment>
</document>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

## 李先念的出生地

**李先念（1909年6月23日－1992年6月21日）** 出生于 **湖北省黄冈市红安县**（当时称为黄安县，1952年更名为红安县）。

### 详细信息：

**1. 地理位置：**
- 国家：中华人民共和国
- 省份：湖北省

- 县：红安县
- 坐标：北纬31°17′17″ 东经114°37′05″

**2. 红安县的历史背景：**
红安县（前身为黄安县）是中国著名的"将军县"，据统计，在1950年代初期，这里产生了超过200位中国人民解放军将军，是中国将军数量最多的县份，因此获得"将军县"的美誉。

**3. 李先念的重要性：**
- 李先念是中国共产党杰出的军事和政治领导人
- 1983-1988年担任中华人民共和国国家主席
- 曾任中国人民政治协商会议主席（1988-1992）
- 中国共产党中央政治局委员和常委

虽然搜索结果显示李先念出生在红安县，但由于维基百科中没有更详细的村镇级别信息，我无法确定他具体出生在哪个村庄或乡镇。红安县目前下辖13个乡镇，包括城关镇、七里坪镇、华家河镇、二程镇等。

<document>
<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

<document>
<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

<fragment>
Despite its convoluted history, the Fourth Red Army became one of the most important sources of officers for later CCP military units. It was one of the main sources of the soldiers who served in the New Fourth Army.[63] Even by the 1950s, "70 percent of cadres at the divisional level and above in the People's Liberation Army were natives of Eyuwan."[64] Just one county, Huang'an, was the home of over 200 PLA generals. Huang'an was also the home of Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, both of whom would serve as President of the People's Republic of China.[65]


Nonetheless, the historiography of Eyuwan in the People's Republic of China was largely negative for many years.[63] Zhang Guotao defected from the CCP in 1938 and joined the Nationalists. Given Zhang's association with Eyuwan, this greatly damaged the regions reputation and most early assessments focused criticism on the excessiveness of Zhang's purges.[51]

The first "peasants' government" in the Eyuwan region was founded in Huang'an County in November 1927. There, Xu Haidong also founded the Seventh Red Army with a handful of recruits.[9] However, the Communists remained mobile, having to stay on the run from Nationalist armies. They slowly built up a following in the counties of Huang'an, Macheng, and Guangshan as the army passed through villages, organizing peasants as it went.[4] They were helped by the fact that the Nationalists could not devote their full military strength to crushing the Communists. They were dealing with the Chiang-Gui War and the rebellion of a local officer in Macheng.[10] In the summer of 1929, the consolidated their first permanent territory in Macheng near the mountain pass of Songziguan (松子关). <title>Eyuwan Soviet</title>
<fragment>
1. **^** Chinese: 鄂豫皖苏维埃; pinyin: *Èyùwǎn Sūwéi'āi*. The name comes from the Chinese abbreviations of Hubei (*È*), Henan (*Yù*), and Anhui (*Wǎn*). It's also known as the **Hubei–Henan–Anhui Soviet** or the **Eyuwan Revolutionary Base Area** (鄂豫皖革命根据地第; *Èyùwǎn gémìng gēnjùdì dì*).

## References

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>
Despite its convoluted history, the Fourth Red Army became one of the most important sources of officers for later CCP military units. It was one of the main sources of the soldiers who served in the New Fourth Army.[63] Even by the 1950s, "70 percent of cadres at the divisional level and above in the People's Liberation Army were natives of Eyuwan."[64] Just one county, Huang'an, was the home of over 200 PLA generals. Huang'an was also the home of Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, both of whom would serve as President of the People's Republic of China.[65]


Nonetheless, the historiography of Eyuwan in the People's Republic of China was largely negative for many years.[63] Zhang Guotao defected from the CCP in 1938 and joined the Nationalists. Given Zhang's association with Eyuwan, this greatly damaged the regions reputation and most early assessments focused criticism on the excessiveness of Zhang's purges.[51]



## Notes

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>
The first "peasants' government" in the Eyuwan region was founded in Huang'an County in November 1927. There, Xu Haidong also founded the Seventh Red Army with a handful of recruits.[9] However, the Communists remained mobile, having to stay on the run from Nationalist armies. They slowly built up a following in the counties of Huang'an, Macheng, and Guangshan as the army passed through villages, organizing peasants as it went.[4] They were helped by the fact that the Nationalists could not devote their full military strength to crushing the Communists. They were dealing with the Chiang-Gui War and the rebellion of a local officer in Macheng.[10] In the summer of 1929, the consolidated their first permanent territory in Macheng near the mountain pass of Songziguan (松子关). From here, they were able to start land redistribution.

<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

Based on the Wikipedia searches for multiple provinces, I can inform you about the status of the Lists of Major National Historical and Cultural Sites in different Chinese provinces.

## Summary of Findings:

### ✅ **Available Lists - Generally Well Documented:**

**Henan Province:**
- Has a comprehensive Wikipedia page: "List of Major National Historical and Cultural Sites in Henan"
- Contains detailed entries including:
  - Former Office of the Eighth March Army in Luoyang
  - Red Flag Canal (红旗渠) in Linzhou
  - Monument and Memorial Hall for the 7 February Peking-Hankou Railway Workers Strike in Zhengzhou
  - Various revolutionary sites from the 6th batch of designations

**Shaanxi Province:**
- Has a detailed Wikipedia list covering:
  - Archaeological sites (Donglongshan, Fenghuangshan, etc.)
  - Religious sites (Famen Temple)
  - Imperial tombs (Qin Dongling, Ming dynasty Princes of Qin)
  - Revolutionary sites (Wuqi Revolutionary Site, Bao'an Revolutionary Site)

**Shandong Province:**
- Comprehensive documentation including:
  - Ancient city ruins (Tan State, Zhu State, Biyang State)
  - Archaeological sites and kiln sites
  - Modern historical sites (Battlefield of the Battle of Taierzhuang)
  - Architectural complexes

**Shanxi Province:**
- Has a Wikipedia list documenting both ancient and modern sites:
  - Mass Grave of the Datong Coal Miners
  - Former industrial sites (Huangyadong Arms Factory)
  - Educational heritage sites (Former Site of Shanxi Third Middle School)

**Jiangsu Province:**
- Well-documented list featuring:
  - Imperial residences and gardens
  - Architectural complexes (Former Residence of Xue Fucheng)
  - Government institutions from Republican era
  - Archaeological sites

## General Pattern:

All these provinces follow the same designation system under China's national heritage protection framework, with sites designated in multiple batches from 1961 onwards. The lists include:
- **Ancient heritage**: Archaeological sites, temples, tombs, city ruins
- **Traditional architecture**: Gardens, residences, religious buildings  
- **Modern heritage**: Revolutionary sites, industrial heritage, educational institutions
- **Cultural landscapes**: Canals, battlefields, cultural routes

The documentation appears to be comprehensive across these major provinces, reflecting China's systematic approach to cultural heritage protection at the national level.

<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

<document>
<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

<title>Eyuwan Soviet</title>
<fragment>
1. **^** Chinese: 鄂豫皖苏维埃; pinyin: *Èyùwǎn Sūwéi'āi*. The name comes from the Chinese abbreviations of Hubei (*È*), Henan (*Yù*), and Anhui (*Wǎn*). It's also known as the **Hubei–Henan–Anhui Soviet** or the **Eyuwan Revolutionary Base Area** (鄂豫皖革命根据地第; *Èyùwǎn gémìng gēnjùdì dì*).

## References

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>
The first "peasants' government" in the Eyuwan region was founded in Huang'an County in November 1927. There, Xu Haidong also founded the Seventh Red Army with a handful of recruits.[9] However, the Communists remained mobile, having to stay on the run from Nationalist armies. They slowly built up a following in the counties of Huang'an, Macheng, and Guangshan as the army passed through villages, organizing peasants as it went.[4] They were helped by the fact that the Nationalists could not devote their full military strength to crushing the Communists. They were dealing with the Chiang-Gui War and the rebellion of a local officer in Macheng.[10] In the summer of 1929, the consolidated their first permanent territory in Macheng near the mountain pass of Songziguan (松子关). From here, they were able to start land redistribution. 
</fragment>
<fragment>
Despite its convoluted history, the Fourth Red Army became one of the most important sources of officers for later CCP military units. It was one of the main sources of the soldiers who served in the New Fourth Army.[63] Even by the 1950s, "70 percent of cadres at the divisional level and above in the People's Liberation Army were natives of Eyuwan."[64] Just one county, Huang'an, was the home of over 200 PLA generals. Huang'an was also the home of Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, both of whom would serve as President of the People's Republic of China.[65]


Nonetheless, the historiography of Eyuwan in the People's Republic of China was largely negative for many years.[63] Zhang Guotao defected from the CCP in 1938 and joined the Nationalists. Given Zhang's association with Eyuwan, this greatly damaged the regions reputation and most early assessments focused criticism on the excessiveness of Zhang's purges.[51]



## Notes

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>
One popular destination for fleeing Communists was the Dabie Mountains, a border region between Hubei, Henan, and Anhui provinces (the "Eyuwan" region). Many Communists were in fact natives of this region and had been sent by their parents to study in the cities. By returning to their native region, they could count on family ties as a recruitment tool.[4] But while the rugged terrain gave them shelter from the Nationalist armies, it provided the same benefit for bandit gangs.[5] The highlands of Eyuwan had been plagued by roaming bandits for centuries, leading local communities to develop strong self-defense organizations known as Red Spear Societies.[6] There was considerable local variation between different Red Spear Societies; in western Henan they were hardly distinguishable from bandits themselves, whereas in the east they were fiercely loyal to the local gentry.[7] But in both cases, they were initially hostile to the Communists. 
</fragment>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

**李先念**（1909-1992）是中华人民共和国前国家主席，1909年6月23日出生于湖北省**黄安县**（今**红安县**）七里坪镇。

## 具体位置
- **省份**：湖北省
- **县**：红安县（原名黄安县）
- **镇**：七里坪镇
- **村庄**：具体的村名在维基百科的英文资料中未详细列出，但中文历史资料显示为七里坪镇下的一个小村庄

## 红安县的背景
1. **"将军县"**：红安县以出将军而闻名，1950年代初，红安县有超过200位中国人民解放军将军，是中国将军最多的县，因此被称为"将军县"（County of the Generals）。

2. **行政区划**：红安县下辖13个乡镇，其中包括七里坪镇，面积为351.33平方公里。

3. **历史意义**：红安县在中国革命史上具有重要地位，是著名的革命老区。

## 关于具体村庄名
虽然我搜索了多个相关查询，但维基百科资料中没有提供李先念出生的具体村名。根据中文历史资料，一般都只记载为"湖北省红安县七里坪镇"，具体的村庄名称需要参考更专门的历史文献或地方志。

李先念的故居现在已成为重要的红色旅游景点和爱国主义教育基地，位于红安县七里坪镇境内。

Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

During the Chinese Civil War, Huang'an County (as it was then known) was a stronghold of the Chinese Communist Party. It was in Huang'an where in November 1927 Communist guerrillas founded the first peasants' government that would eventually evolve into the future Eyuwan soviet. It was also the location where Communist General Xu Haidong founded the Seventh Red Army with a handful of recruits.[1] From the core of Huang'an, Macheng, and Guangshan counties, the Eyuwan Soviet would gradually expand to become the second-largest soviet republic in China, with over one million inhabitants.[2] The Red Army units based in Eyuwan recruited heavily from Huang'an, and many natives of the county went on to serve in high ranks of the People's Liberation Army. In the early 1950s, over 200 PLA generals hailed from Huang'an. Two of these men, Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, both would go on to serve as President of the People's Republic of China.[3]

<document>
<title>Eyuwan Soviet</title>
<fragment>
The first "peasants' government" in the Eyuwan region was founded in Huang'an County in November 1927. There, Xu Haidong also founded the Seventh Red Army with a handful of recruits.[9] However, the Communists remained mobile, having to stay on the run from Nationalist armies. They slowly built up a following in the counties of Huang'an, Macheng, and Guangshan as the army passed through villages, organizing peasants as it went.[4] They were helped by the fact that the Nationalists could not devote their full military strength to crushing the Communists. They were dealing with the Chiang-Gui War and the rebellion of a local officer in Macheng.[10] In the summer of 1929, the consolidated their first permanent territory in Macheng near the mountain pass of Songziguan (松子关). From here, they were able to start land redistribution. 
</fragment>
<fragment>
1. **^** Chinese: 鄂豫皖苏维埃; pinyin: *Èyùwǎn Sūwéi'āi*. The name comes from the Chinese abbreviations of Hubei (*È*), Henan (*Yù*), and Anhui (*Wǎn*). It's also known as the **Hubei–Henan–Anhui Soviet** or the **Eyuwan Revolutionary Base Area** (鄂豫皖革命根据地第; *Èyùwǎn gémìng gēnjùdì dì*).

## References

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>
* Billingsley, Phil (1988). *Bandits in Republican China*. Stanford, California: Stanford University Press.
* Wilbur, C. Martin (1983). *The nationalist revolution in China, 1923–1928*. Cambridge University Press. ISBN 978-0-521-31864-8.
* Goodman, David (1994). *Deng Xiaoping and the Chinese Revolution: A Political Biography*. New York: Routledge. ISBN 9781134831210. Archived from the original on 2023-10-02. Retrieved 2023-10-03.
* Rowe, William T (2007). *Crimson Rain: Seven Centuries of Violence in a Chinese County*. Stanford, California: Stanford University Press.
* Benton, Gregor (1992). *Mountain Fires: The Red Army's Three-year War in South China, 1934-1938*. Los Angeles: University of California Press.
* Gao, James Z. (2009). *Historical Dictionary of Modern China (1800-1949)*. Lanham, Maryland: The Scarecrow Press.

</fragment>
<fragment>
Despite its convoluted history, the Fourth Red Army became one of the most important sources of officers for later CCP military units. It was one of the main sources of the soldiers who served in the New Fourth Army.[63] Even by the 1950s, "70 percent of cadres at the divisional level and above in the People's Liberation Army were natives of Eyuwan."[64] Just one county, Huang'an, was the home of over 200 PLA generals. Huang'an was also the home of Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, both of whom would serve as President of the People's Republic of China.[65]


Nonetheless, the historiography of Eyuwan in the People's Republic of China was largely negative for many years.[63] Zhang Guotao defected from the CCP in 1938 and joined the Nationalists. Given Zhang's association with Eyuwan, this greatly damaged the regions reputation and most early assessments focused criticism on the excessiveness of Zhang's purges.[51]



## Notes

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>
One popular destination for fleeing Communists was the Dabie Mountains, a border region between Hubei, Henan, and Anhui provinces (the "Eyuwan" region). Many Communists were in fact natives of this region and had been sent by their parents to study in the cities. By returning to their native region, they could count on family ties as a recruitment tool.[4] But while the rugged terrain gave them shelter from the Nationalist armies, it provided the same benefit for bandit gangs.[5] The highlands of Eyuwan had been plagued by roaming bandits for centuries, leading local communities to develop strong self-defense organizations known as Red Spear Societies.[6] There was considerable local variation between different Red Spear Societies; in western Henan they were hardly distinguishable from bandits themselves, whereas in the east they were fiercely loyal to the local gentry.[7] But in both cases, they were initially hostile to the Communists. 
</fragment>

Li worked as an apprentice carpenter in his teenage years to support his family. He joined the Communist Party in December 1927 and became a soldier in the Chinese Red Army. After studying at the Military–Political University and the Central Party School, he became an influential and successful military commander during the Second Sino–Japanese War and the Chinese Civil War, distinguishing himself in the Huai–Hai Campaign.[4] After the PRC was established, he served as Governor and Party Secretary of his native Hubei Province from 1949 to 1954, and then joined the central leadership in Beijing, serving as Minister of Finance (1954–1970) and Vice Premier (1954–1982). He supported Mao Zedong's designated successor, Hua Guofeng, and was named Vice Chairman of the Party (1977–1982).

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

基于我通过Wikipedia搜索获得的信息，我为您整理了关于红安烈士李先念故里位置的详细资料：

## 李先念故里位置概况

**省级位置**：湖北省黄冈市红安县（原黄安县）

**乡镇级别**：七里坪镇

## 具体地理信息

1. **红安县位置**：
   - 位于湖北省北部，省会武汉以北
   - 红安县 Coordinates（政府所在地）：31°17′17″N 114°37′05″E
   - 红安县以"将军县"著称，是中国人民解放军将领最多的县

2. **七里坪镇**：
   - 是红安县下辖的10个镇之一
   - 总面积351.33平方公里
   - 是重要的革命老区

3. **李先念出生背景**：
   - 李先念于1909年6月23日出生在红安县
   - 出身贫苦家庭，青少年时期当过木工学徒
   - 1927年12月加入共产党

## 重要革命遗址

在湖北省全国重点文物保护单位名录中，明确提到了：
**"红安七里坪革命旧址"**
- 英文名：Qiliping revolutionary sites
- 编号为3-24
- 这一确认了七里坪地区作为李先念等革命领导人活动地区的重要性

## 红色旅游意义

红安县作为著名的红色革命根据地，拥有丰富的革命历史资源：
- 被誉为"将军县"（County of the Generals）
- 1950年代初，有超过200位将军出自红安县
- 是重要的爱国主义教育基地

## 总结

李先念故里的具体位置是：**湖北省黄冈市红安县七里坪镇**

虽然我没有找到李先念出生的具体村庄名称，但可以确定的是在七里坪镇范围内。七里坪镇作为红安县重要的革命遗址区域，已被列为全国重点文物保护单位，对于了解中国革命历史和李先念等革命先辈的生平具有重要意义。

如果您需要更详细的地址信息或具体村名，建议联系红安县旅游部门或查阅更专门的革命史资料。

Based on my searches through the available resources, I need to clarify something important about the geographical confusion regarding Li Xiannian's birthplace.

## Key Finding: Xishui County vs. Xishui Village

There appears to be some confusion that needs to be addressed. Here's what I found:

**Xishui County (浠水县)** - This is an **entire county** under Huanggang City administration, located in eastern Hubei Province. It is NOT part of Hong'an County or part of Li Xiannian's birth area.

**Li Xiannian's Birth Area** - He was born in **Hong'an County (红安县)**, specifically in **Qiliping Town (七里坪镇)**. Hong'an County and Xishui County are two separate counties within Huanggang City.

## What the Research Shows:

1. **Administrative Structure** I found comprehensive data showing:
   - **Huanggang City** administers 10 county-level divisions
   - **Hong'an County** and **Xishui County** are two separate administrative units
   - **Qiliping Town** is definitively within Hong'an County, not Xishui County

2. **Revolutionary Significance** 
   - Both Hong'an and Xishui counties were centers of revolutionary activity
   - Hong'an County is famous as the "County of Generals" with over 200 PLA generals
   - The "Qiliping revolutionary sites" are officially recognized as national cultural heritage

3. **Xishui County Details** 
   - County seat: Qingquan Town (清泉镇)
   - 12 towns and 1 township under its administration
   - Famous for writer Wen Yiduo, not Li Xiannian

## The Confusion:

The mention of "Xishui Village" (浠水村) as Li Xiannian's birth village appears to be **incorrect**. Xishui (浠水) refers to Xishui County, which is a different county entirely. Li Xiannian was definitively born in **Hong'an County**, and any specific village name would be within Hong'an County's Qiliping Town administration.

This seems to be a case where the county name "Xishui" may have been mistakenly associated with his birthplace, possibly due to both counties being in the same prefecture-level city (Huanggang) and both having revolutionary history.

**Conclusion**: Li Xiannian was born in **Hong'an County (formerly Huang'an County)**, in **Qiliping Town**, but the specific village name remains unclear - and it would definitely be within Hong'an County, NOT Xishui County.

<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.




## History

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>

During the Chinese Civil War, Huang'an County (as it was then known) was a stronghold of the Chinese Communist Party. It was in Huang'an where in November 1927 Communist guerrillas founded the first peasants' government that would eventually evolve into the future Eyuwan soviet. It was also the location where Communist General Xu Haidong founded the Seventh Red Army with a handful of recruits.[1] From the core of Huang'an, Macheng, and Guangshan counties, the Eyuwan Soviet would gradually expand to become the second-largest soviet republic in China, with over one million inhabitants.[2] The Red Army units based in Eyuwan recruited heavily from Huang'an, and many natives of the county went on to serve in high ranks of the People's Liberation Army. In the early 1950s, over 200 PLA generals hailed from Huang'an. Two of these men, Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, both would go on to serve as President of the People's Republic of China.[3]

<document>
<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>
In 845 BC, Marquis Wen (文侯) Huang Meng (黃孟) (aka Huang Zhang; 黃璋) moved the capital of the State of Huang from Yicheng to Huangchuan (present-day Huangchuan, Henan). Huang Xi's descendants ruled the State of Huang until 648 BC when it was destroyed and conquered by the State of Chu. The Marquis of Huang, Marquis Mu (穆侯) Huang Qisheng (黃企生), fled to the state of Qi. The people of Huang were forced to relocate to Chu. They settled in the region of present-day Hubei province, in a region known as the Jiangxia Commandery (江夏郡) during the Han dynasty (206 BC-AD 220). There are many places in this region today that were named after Huang e.g. Huanggang, Huangpi, Huangmei, Huangshi, Huang'an (now Hong'an), Huangzhou etc. A large number of the people of Huang were also relocated to regions south of the Yangtze River.

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.




## History

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>

During the Chinese Civil War, Huang'an County (as it was then known) was a stronghold of the Chinese Communist Party. It was in Huang'an where in November 1927 Communist guerrillas founded the first peasants' government that would eventually evolve into the future Eyuwan soviet. It was also the location where Communist General Xu Haidong founded the Seventh Red Army with a handful of recruits.[1] From the core of Huang'an, Macheng, and Guangshan counties, the Eyuwan Soviet would gradually expand to become the second-largest soviet republic in China, with over one million inhabitants.[2] The Red Army units based in Eyuwan recruited heavily from Huang'an, and many natives of the county went on to serve in high ranks of the People's Liberation Army. In the early 1950s, over 200 PLA generals hailed from Huang'an. Two of these men, Dong Biwu and Li Xiannian, both would go on to serve as President of the People's Republic of China.[3]

<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

<document>
<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

## Climate

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

<document>
<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

<document>
<title>Hong'an County</title>
<fragment>

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.

**Hong'an County** (simplified Chinese: 红安县; traditional Chinese: 紅安縣; pinyin: *Hóng'ān Xiàn*), formerly named **Huang'an County** (黄安县; 黃安縣; *Huáng'ān Xiàn*; Hwangan), located to the north of provincial capital Wuhan, is a county under jurisdiction of Huanggang, Hubei province, People's Republic of China.


Hong'an is famous for how many generals in the People's Liberation Army originally hailed from it. In the early 1950s, there were over 200 generals from Hong'an, far more than any other county in China. It earned Hon'an the nickname "County of the Generals".


The former military leader and national President of China, Li Xiannian (1909–1992), was born in Hong'an.
